extraction_warnings: This paper is a large metagenomic assembly study that reports aggregate statistics across 9,428 metagenomes from 46 datasets. Individual sample-level metadata are not provided in the main text or methods section. Sample-level data would require access to supplementary tables (Table S1 mentioned but not fully provided in extracted text) or external databases (curatedMetagenomicData, NCBI-SRA).

The granularity is marked as 'sample_level' per the schema requirement, but the paper reports study-level and subgroup-level aggregates, not per-sample rows. No individual sample metadata extraction is possible from the provided text.

Age is reported only by category (newborns <1 year: 1,098 samples; children ≥1 and <12 years: 465 samples; school-age ≥12 and <19 years: 216 samples; adults ≥19 years: 6,615 samples; 46 samples missing metadata) at aggregate level, not per sample.
Westernization status is reported as study-level aggregates (592 non-Westernized, 8,836 Westernized samples total) but individual sample assignments are not provided in text.
Country information is provided as study-level summaries (USA 1,431 samples, China 1,342, Israel 956, Sweden 600, Denmark 580 are top 5) but not per-sample in the provided sections.
Body site is reported as aggregate counts (7,783 gut, 783 oral, 503 skin, 88 vagina, 9 milk samples) but not assigned to individual samples in provided text.

This paper is a metagenomic diversity catalog study describing 154,723 microbial genomes from human samples. The schema provided is designed for clinical trial/oncology studies with patient-level health outcomes (disease response, tumor staging, biomarkers, etc.). None of these fields are applicable to this microbiome genomics paper, which focuses on microbial genome reconstruction, annotation, and prevalence across diverse populations and body sites. All extracted values are 'not_reported' as expected.

sequencing_platform: Study integrated data from 46 public datasets with potentially heterogeneous sequencing platforms; value reported applies only to newly sequenced Madagascar and Ethiopian cohorts.
